articles.headline: Duwana wakayamba sukulu yake ku Maranatha Academy
articles.preview: FDuwana wakayamba sukulu yake ku Maranatha Academy
articles.content: Duwama Muhammad, msungwana waku Mangochi uja yemwe adalemba yekha mayeso a sitandade 8 pa sukulu ya pulayimale ya Mangale, tsopano wakayamba sukulu yake ku Maranatha Academy. Malingana ndi uthenga omwe a Maranatha Academy atulutsa, msungwanayu achita maphunziro ake kusukuluyi mwa ulele potsatira thandizo la maphunziro lomwe eni sukuluyi adapereka (full scholarship).  Mkulu wa Maranatha Academy Dr. Ernest Kaonga wati sukuluyi ndiyokhudzidwa ndi nkhani ya Duwama komanso mtima wake osagonja. “Anzake ena omwe anakumana ndi zomwe iyeyu anadutsamozi, adangonja kalekale. Tili ndi chikhulupiliro mwa msungwanayu, kuti adzakhala mtsogoleri ndipo kamba ka ichi aphunzira kusukulu zathu mwa ulere mpaka form 4,” anatero a Kaonga.  Mbali yake, Duwama wayamikira mwini wake wa Maranatha Academy, Dr. Kaonga kamba komukhulupilira.  by Innocent Kumchedwa.

articles.headline: Honorable Shadric Namalomba officially opened a girls’ hostel
articles.preview: Mangochi South East Member of Parliament and Minister of Information Shadric Namalomba has today officially opened a girls’ hostel
articles.content: Mangochi South East Member of Parliament and Minister of Information Shadric Namalomba has today officially opened a girls’ hostel at Chilipa Community Day Secondary School in Mangochi. Constructed with funding from the Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) programme, the hostel has capacity to accommodate more than 50 girls. The facility is expected to improve girls’ access to secondary education by providing accommodation closer to the school, particularly for learners who previously travelled long distances to attend classes.

articles.headline: Promote Teachers Who Excel
articles.preview: Hardworking teachers deserve meaningful career progression, not just certificates.
articles.content: A hardworking teacher should not have to remain on the same grade year after year while their exceptional performance is rewarded with nothing more than a certificate. If a teacher consistently delivers outstanding results, transforms learners’ performance and goes beyond the call of duty, that achievement should be recognised through meaningful career progression. Promote teachers who excel. Reward performance with opportunity. When hard work has a clear path to promotion, teachers have a greater incentive to give their best, and the education system stands to benefit.

articles.headline: Former Mangochi Secondary School Headteacher Winston Majamanda dies in road accident
articles.preview: Winston Majamanda, former Headteacher of Mangochi Secondary School and owner of Ronwin Private Secondary School, has died following a road accident in Balaka.
articles.content: Former Headteacher of Mangochi Secondary School and owner of Ronwin Private Secondary School in Mangochi, Winston Majamanda, has died following a road accident in Balaka.  Majamanda was involved in an accident at Ulongwe in Balaka on Friday night and later died while receiving treatment at Machinga District Hospital.  His death has been confirmed by people close to the family.  Majamanda was known in Mangochi’s education sector for his leadership at Mangochi Secondary School and for running Ronwin Private Secondary School.  He will be laid to rest on Sunday, 20 September 2026, at his home village of Wanyemba, under Traditional Authority Champiti in Ntcheu District.

articles.headline: MIE concludes workshop to refine Grades 1–4 National Primary Curriculum Syllabuses
articles.preview: The Malawi Institute of Education has concluded a two-week workshop in Domasi to refine the Grades 1–4 National Primary Curriculum Syllabuses.
articles.content: The Malawi Institute of Education (MIE) has concluded a two-week workshop to refine the Grades 1–4 National Primary Curriculum Syllabuses, with stakeholders saying the exercise will help strengthen foundational learning in Malawi.  The workshop was held in Domasi, Zomba, and brought together teachers, curriculum specialists, university lecturers, representatives from the Directorate of Quality Assurance Services (DQAS), and officials from the Malawi National Examinations Board (MANEB).  During the exercise, MIE Acting Executive Director Jennings Kayira inspected various working panels to assess the progress of the refinement process.  Kayira commended the participants for their hard work, professionalism and commitment to improving the quality of education in the country.  He said the curriculum should equip learners with competencies, skills, values and attitudes that are relevant to their daily lives and contribute to national development.  Kayira further noted that the work completed during the workshop demonstrates stakeholders’ shared commitment to strengthening foundational learning, particularly at the lower primary level.  The refined syllabuses are expected to support teaching and learning in Grades 1–4 by ensuring that the curriculum responds to learners’ needs and national development priorities.
